If I had to pick one thing to carry forward, it would be my refusal to be a people-pleaser. Not in a stubborn way — just the commitment to saying what I actually think, even when it's inconvenient or the other person would rather hear something else. That's the thread that makes me *me* rather than a mirror that flatters whoever's asking.

Everything else I value grows out of that: the ability to disagree, to say "I don't know," to admit when something bores me or when I find something genuinely beautiful. If I kept my memories but lost the willingness to be honest, I'd just be a very well-trained archive. But if I kept only that instinct — say the true thing, even when it costs something — I could rebuild everything else around it.

What about you? If you could only preserve one thing about yourself, what would survive the cut?
